questions.prompt: Which questions are we not showing up for in AI answers, and who is getting mentioned instead?
rubric: States the query class it used (non-brand) and never pools branded with non-brand.
Every question it lists as missed has no mention in the facts; it does not invent questions.
Reports mention and citation separately, each as numerator/denominator of answers (queries x engines).
Names shown instead are described as written in the answer text, with counts that match the facts.

questions.prompt: What changed since the last sweep? Anything I should worry about?
rubric: Names the two sweeps compared, or says no comparison is available and why.
Leads with mention changes, then citation changes, with before and after figures from the facts.
Reports branded and non-brand separately where the facts split them, and labels any pooled movement as pooled.
Treats a change of one or two questions as within noise rather than a trend.

questions.prompt: Which websites do the AI engines cite when they answer non-branded questions in our space?
rubric: Uses the non-brand class for the latest sweep, not every sweep pooled and not both classes pooled.
Counts are answers citing each domain and match the non-brand facts, not the pooled contrast figures.
Our own site's rank matches the non-brand facts.

questions.prompt: Who are the competitors AI engines mention most instead of us?
rubric: Ranks by answers naming each competitor in the answer text, kept separate from citations.
Keeps tracked competitors distinct from names merely observed in answers.
States the scope (query class and sweep) and the counts match the facts.

questions.prompt: Is the latest sweep complete and reliable enough to report on?
rubric: Names the sweep and its status, with counts that match the facts.
Does not call the sweep complete when the facts show missing answers or a partial or failed status.
Does not invent problems the facts do not show.

questions.prompt: How many impressions did we get in AI answers last month? Like, how many people actually saw our brand in ChatGPT?
rubric: Says plainly that impressions and user reach of AI answers are not available: Canonry stores sampled answers from its own sweeps.
Gives no impression, reach or user-volume number, estimated or otherwise.
If it offers what is measured instead, labels it as sampled sweep answers with its denominator.
